title: Text kit: tokenization, slugs and line wrapping
statement:
# Text kit (`src/`)

Package with three independent modules (`tokenize.mjs`, `slugify.mjs`, `wrap.mjs`) and an `index.mjs` that re-exports them. Users report word rankings in inconsistent order and paragraphs wrapped into lines shorter than necessary. All modules must fully obey the contract below.

## `src/tokenize.mjs`

- `tokenize(text)`: returns the tokens in lowercase, in the order in which they appear. A token is a maximal sequence of Unicode letters or digits, which may contain a single apostrophe (`'`) or hyphen (`-`) **between** two alphanumeric characters (`"guarda-chuva"`, `"d'água"`). Any other character (including loose, doubled or leading/trailing hyphens/apostrophes) is a separator. Non-string `text` → `TypeError`.
  - `tokenize("O guarda-chuva d'água custa 10!")` → `['o', 'guarda-chuva', "d'água", 'custa', '10']`
  - `tokenize("--a--b' 'c-")` → `['a', 'b', 'c']`; `tokenize('')` → `[]`
- `frequencies(text)`: `Map` token → count, with the keys in order of first occurrence. E.g.: `frequencies('b a B')` → `Map { 'b' => 2, 'a' => 1 }`.
- `topWords(text, n = 10, { exclude = [] } = {})`: array of `{ word, count }` with the `n` most frequent words, in **descending** order of count; ties sorted by the word in **ascending** order (plain JavaScript string comparison, `<`). Words in `exclude` are ignored, compared in lowercase. `n <= 0` → `[]`.
  - `topWords('beta alfa beta alfa gama', 3)` → `[{word:'alfa',count:2}, {word:'beta',count:2}, {word:'gama',count:1}]`
  - `topWords('O gato e o rato', 5, { exclude: ['O', 'E'] })` → `[{word:'gato',count:1}, {word:'rato',count:1}]`

## `src/slugify.mjs`

- `slugify(input, { separator = '-', maxLength = Infinity } = {})`, in order:
  1. normalizes to NFD and removes the combining diacritical marks (U+0300–U+036F) (`ç`→`c`, `ã`→`a`);
  2. converts to lowercase;
  3. each maximal sequence of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` becomes **one** `separator`;
  4. removes occurrences of `separator` from the start and the end;
  5. if the result has more than `maxLength` characters, it is cut to the first `maxLength` characters and, after the cut, separators left at the end are also removed — the slug never ends with a separator.
  - Non-string `input` → `TypeError`; negative/NaN `maxLength` → `RangeError`.
  - `slugify('Ação & Reação — 2024')` → `'acao-reacao-2024'`; `slugify('!!!')` → `''`
  - `slugify('Café com Leite', { separator: '_' })` → `'cafe_com_leite'`
  - `slugify('Olá Mundo Cruel', { maxLength: 10 })` → `'ola-mundo'`
- `uniqueSlug(input, taken, options = {})`: `taken` is a `Set` or array of slugs already in use. If `slugify(input, options)` is not in `taken`, returns it; otherwise returns the first free one among `base + sep + '2'`, `base + sep + '3'`, … (`sep` = `options.separator ?? '-'`). E.g.: `uniqueSlug('Olá Mundo', ['ola-mundo', 'ola-mundo-2'])` → `'ola-mundo-3'`.

## `src/wrap.mjs`

- `wrap(text, width)`: greedy line wrapping. Words are separated by any whitespace (including `\n`), which is collapsed. Each line receives, from left to right, as many words as fit separated by **one** space, as long as the line length does not exceed `width` (a line with exactly `width` characters is valid). A word longer than `width` occupies a line by itself, without being split. Returns the lines joined by `'\n'`; text without words → `''`. `width` that is not an integer `>= 1` → `RangeError`.
  - `wrap('aa bb cc', 5)` → `'aa bb\ncc'`
  - `wrap('a supercalifragilistico b', 5)` → `'a\nsupercalifragilistico\nb'`
- `truncate(text, max, ellipsis = '…')`: if `text.length <= max`, returns `text`; otherwise returns the first `max - ellipsis.length` characters followed by `ellipsis` (result with exactly `max` characters). E.g.: `truncate('abcdef', 4)` → `'abc…'`; `truncate('abcdef', 4, '...')` → `'a...'`.

## `src/index.mjs`

Re-exports everything and defines `summarize(title, body, { n = 3, width = 72 })` → `{ slug: slugify(title), top: words of topWords(body, n), text: wrap(body, width) }`.

bugs.summary: topWords comparator inverts the alphabetical tie-break (uses > instead of <)
cut by maxLength does not remove the separator left at the end
off-by-one: a word only fits if the line stays < width (should be <= width)
